query.comment: NF-5 (reliability): the system never stops for a software reason. FAILS TODAY. Trace: mash 2 h -> lauter 2 h -> boil 1 h, then at t = 5 Scheduling sits in a committed location waiting to send start_whirlpool! and Whirlpooling has no transitions, so nobody receives it. Even after the whirlpool exists this will fail again when all tanks are busy, because the location before start_maturation_fermentation! is committed and time cannot pass there. That location must become a normal one.
Sanity: at least one batch can go through all seven steps and be filtered. FAILS TODAY, same cause as the deadlock (empty Whirlpooling).
Sanity: cold wort reaches a tank at all. FAILS TODAY (empty Whirlpooling). Until this holds, every property about tanks below is vacuously true.

Precondition for NF-8 (95 % tank usage): two batches ferment at the same time in two tanks. FAILS TODAY. Needs the whirlpool AND a scheduler that releases the next batch while the previous one is still in a tank.
FR-4.1: mashing never runs longer than T_MASHING. The guard c >= T_MASHING on the exit edge gives the lower bound, so together the stage lasts exactly T_MASHING hours. Holds.
FR-4.2: lautering lasts exactly T_LAUTER hours (invariant + guard x == T_LAUTER). Holds.
FR-10: sweet wort leaves the kettle as hot wort 1 hour after entering (T_BOILING = 1). Holds since PR #4; before it the invariant was c <= 60, i.e. 60 hours, with no lower bound.
Fermentation phase of a tank lasts at most 120 h = 5 days. Vacuously true today (tanks unreachable, see E<> tank1.Fermentation).
FR-10: beer is transferred out of the tank 14 days = 336 h after entering (120 h fermentation + 216 h maturation, one clock). Vacuously true today.

query.formula: A[] sweet_wort_batches >= 0 && hot_wort_batches >= 0 && cold_wort_batches >= 0 && green_beer_batches >= 0 && beer_batches >= 0
query.comment: No stage consumes a batch that does not exist (every start guard requires input >= 1). Holds.
The kettle never produces more hot wort than the whirlpool can hold (MAX_HOT_WORT_BATCHES = 1). Holds.
FR-3: every mashed batch is eventually lautered (leads-to). Holds.
FR-3: every lautered batch is eventually boiled. Holds.
FR-3: every boiled batch eventually reaches a tank (via whirlpool). FAILS TODAY (empty Whirlpooling).
FR-3: every matured batch is eventually filtered. Vacuously true today.

DOCUMENTS A LIMITATION, not a goal: with the current Scheduling chain mashing and lautering never overlap, because the next start_mashing! fires only after the previous batch got a tank. Holds today. Once the hot side is pipelined (each stage pulls a batch when input >= 1 and output has room, like Boiling already does) this must become FALSE and the next query must hold.

TARGET: batch N+1 is mashed while batch N is lautered. FAILS TODAY (serial scheduler). Needed for NF-8: with 24 tanks x 14 days, a batch must leave the hot side every ~14.7 h or less, which a serial 5 h chain does, but only if it never waits for a tank.
A tank that holds beer is marked busy, so the scheduler cannot assign it twice. Vacuously true today.
A free tank is not marked busy (flag is released on Maturation -> Wait). Holds.

Bound on the state space. Holds. NOTE: started_batches++ sits on the broadcast edge Wait -> CheckTankIdx that EVERY tank takes, so one batch increments it once per tank instance. Should move to the edge of the chosen tank only.
